To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Fe is a beneficial dopant for Ni/CGO catalysts for SOFC/SOEL cells.
the addition of Fe to Ni/CGO catalysts results in the formation of NiFe alloy, and that the presence of Fe in the catalyst leads to the formation of CeFeO3, GdFeOx and Gd2Fe17.
Fe diffuses into Ni/CGOs during the reduction process and that the diffusion is dependent on the amount of Fe and the size of the oxide nanoparticles.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the effect of Fe on the structure and performance of the catalyst.
the effect of Fe on the high performing Ni/CGO electrocatalysts, which is a crucial step towards the development of low-cost SOFCs.
the effect of Fe on the reduction and sintering of Ni/CGO and the impact on the cell performance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Fe diffusion into CGO during reduction is dependent on both, the Fe loading and CGO particle size, and the Fe loading is a key factor to consider when designing a high performing FeNi/CGODC fuel electrode.
the Fe addition to the Ni/CGO system is not beneficial for the fuel electrode.

the presence of Fe in Ni/CGO catalysts is not recommended for SOFC/SOCE cells, as the presence of Fe will result in a significant increase in particle size, and the formation of Fe oxides, both, detrimental for the cell performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presence of Fe in the catalysts has a detrimental impact on the electrochemical performance of Ni/CGO catalyst.
Fe is not a good addition to Ni/CGO catalysts for SOFC/SOFC electrodes, but that Fe is an interesting addition to Ni/YSZ catalysts.

the addition of Fe to Ni/CGO catalysts is detrimental to the performance of the catalysts in terms of the catalytic activity for H2 oxidation, the stability of the oxide support and to the long term stability of the SOFC/SOCE cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Fe diffuses rapidly through the CGO nanopowder during reduction and the diffusion is enhanced at high metal loadings.
Fe is detrimental for the catalyst performance, which is attributed to the formation of the Fe containing oxides.
the addition of Fe to the catalyst is detrimental for the cell operation.
